title: Strict scalar composition associators and proper/open factor equations
statement: For finite coefficient field inclusions E → F → L: the constant coefficient maps compose; the ordinary, derived-base, whole-tower and strict derived-tower tensor associators and the completed tensor associator are the canonical composite-adjunction comparisons; arithmetic selection of levels e then h is selection of level h*e, and the ramification indices multiply. The strict proper scalar mates compose under the strict tower associator (compositionProper), and so do the open balancing maps (compositionOpen).

source.place: Tags 07A6, 0E8I and 0941; auxiliary strict scalar composition calculations preceding support realization.

proof.text: Unfold constantMap, rewrite composition of the underlying functor maps, and use extensionality of the composed algebra homomorphisms. The ramification equality follows from Ideal.map_map and Ideal.map_pow: if t O_F = v^e O_F and v O_L = w^h O_L then t O_L = (v O_L)^e = w^{he} O_L. The selection identity is for the ramification indices e,h >= 1 (for e = 0 it fails): with index_e(n) = e(n+1)-1 one has index_h(index_e(n)) = h(e(n+1)-1+1)-1 = he(n+1)-1 = index_{he}(n), using e(n+1) >= 1, and arrows agree because the order category of N has at most one arrow between two objects. The ordinary associator is by definition the left-adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism (leftAdjointUniq) of the composite of the two constant scalar adjunctions, transported along the identity-on-sections restriction compositor; the derived-base associator is its exact localization, and the whole-tower associator is its pointwise whiskering over the index category. The strict derived-tower associator (the exact localization of the whole-tower one) is the canonical composite-adjunction comparison leftAdjointCompIso by the cited tower-associator statement; this is a theorem, not a definition.

For the completed tensor associator, write c_{L/F}, c_{F/E}, c_{L/E} for the completed coefficient maps. By the defining uniqueness in the completed scalar data, c_{L/E} is the unique map with pi_{L,n} c_{L/E} = ((j i)_n)_Y pi_{E,n} for every n; and pi_{L,n} c_{L/F} c_{F/E} = (j_n)_Y pi_{F,n} c_{F/E} = (j_n)_Y (i_n)_Y pi_{E,n} = ((j i)_n)_Y pi_{E,n}, since the constant-sheaf functor preserves composition. Hence c_{L/F} c_{F/E} = c_{L/E}. The completed associator is, by definition, the left-adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism of the composite of the two derived completed scalar adjunctions with the adjunction for c_{L/E}, taken along this equality; that is the canonical composite-adjunction comparison the item asserts. The completed-scalar-associator localization statement, applied to the finite coefficient tower, moreover identifies this associator, followed by the completed exact model of the composite, with the successive exact-model comparisons followed by the localized ordinary scalar associator, so the same isomorphism is the one used in the strict and constant descriptions.

proof.text: compositionProper: the strict tower associator is the composite-adjunction comparison (scalarTowerAssociator_normalization). Invert the proved proper-restriction cocycle (properRestriction_composition) and apply mateEquiv_hcomp with the two conjugate/mate pasting identities.

compositionOpen: apply ordinaryBaseOpenTensor_composition at each index of an ordinary strict tower. The strict-scalar-mate statement identifies openTensor with the exact localized ordinaryOpenTensor comparison, and the derived exact-square-composition lemma pastes the resulting natural-isomorphism square through the exact localization. Natural-transformation extensionality then gives the stated equation, including all quotient transitions.
